title: Model Greedy-Admit Queue Capacity Playbook
content:
Purpose:
This playbook captures an operationally focused capacity estimate and gating checklist for a greedy-admit model onboarding flow (i.e., admit as many holders as possible subject to queueing/shaping) with explicit KV cache footprint accounting across regions. Intended as a rapid reference for on-call + infra release engineers when a new medium-to-large model is introduced to hosted and dedicated pools.

Summary (TL;DR):
- Conservative headroom target: 20% free GPU slots per region for first 72h of public rollout.
- KV warmup budget: allocate prefix-prefetching to 0.4–0.6% of regional cache capacity (per tranche) and shadow the remaining 10% of expected warmed keys for 24h.
- Admission heuristic: greedy admit with soft-queue at 90th pct latency breach; hard-throttle at 99.9th pct token-serve CPU/GPU util >= 92%.
- Rollout cadence: 3 tranches (internal-only -> beta customers -> full), each >= 8h and monitor for KV eviction spikes.

Assumptions (input cells):
- New model peak RPS per region (conservative): 12k requests/min (~200 rps).
- Avg tokens per request: 75 (user prompts + safety buffer).
- GPU concurrency slot per request (avg): 0.7 (due to batching).
- Effective KV entry size: 2.4 KB per prefix entry (measured from model variant v3-compact).
- Expected unique prefixes per active session: 7.5
- Session churn factor (new unique prefixes/day): 1.12
- Regional cache capacity (example region-eu-1): 1.2 TB usable for prefix cache.

Quick math (worked example region-eu-1):
- RPS -> tokens/sec: 200 rps * 75 tokens = 15,000 tokens/sec.
- Simultaneous slot demand: concurrency = rps * slot_per_request -> 200 * 0.7 = 140 concurrent slots.
- GPU fleet equivalent slots (slot_per_gpu = 32): 140/32 = 4.375 GPUs -> round up to 5 GPUs.
- Warm prefix budget per tranche: assume 30% of active sessions will warm prefixes within 1h -> expected warm prefixes = active_sessions * 7.5 * 0.3. If active_sessions approximated as rps*60*user_hang_time(=2.5m) -> 200*150 = 30k sessions -> warm prefixes = 30k * 7.5 * 0.3 = 67,500 prefixes -> KV bytes = 67,500 * 2.4 KB = ~162 MB.
- Note: the warm prefix budget scales faster with session hang time than rps.

KV occupancy scenarios (table-style rows):
- Minimal warmup (no prefetch): 10–12% cache churn increase, eviction latency spike risk = medium.
- Conservative prefetch (our recommended default): prefetch up to 0.5% of region usable cache for early tranches; eviction churn delta = 3–5%.
- Aggressive prefetch (experimental): prefetch 2–3% cache -> eviction churn delta = 15–22% (not recommended unless slot headroom >40%).

Queueing/admission policy heuristics:
1) Soft-queue (SLO breach detector): if 90th pct tail latency for token serve crosses 1.5x target, route new model requests to a short 10s queue. Queue should surface metrics: depth, avg wait, dequeue rate.
2) Model-pool fallback: after 40s in queue, attempt fallback to quantized variant if available (q4_0 or q4_1) and mark metric as fallback_count.
3) Hard-throttle: if GPU mean util >= 92% sustained for 120s and KV eviction rate > baseline by 3x, block new model admits until either util drops <88% or eviction normalizes.

Operational checklist (pre-rollout):
- [ ] Run local warmup shadow run (JIRA-ENG-4123) against a copied cache bucket for 6h. Capture eviction rate baseline.
- [ ] Provision staging tranche capacity (5 GPUs region-eu-1 in example) + reserve 20% burst capacity.
- [ ] Configure prefetch controller: set prefetch_limit=0.005*usable_cache for tranche 1; toggle off for tranche 3.
- [ ] Create canary traffic generator job (k8s job: infra/canary/new-model-loadtest) with 3 traffic profiles: internal_dev, beta_customers, public_preview.
- [ ] Add monitoring boards: token-serve latency (p50/p90/p99), queue depth, KV eviction/sec, KV memory usage, GPU util per-host.

Tranche schedule template (recommended):
- Tranche 0 – internal: 2h, 5–10% seed traffic, engineers on-call.
- Tranche 1 – beta customers: 8–12h, 25% of expected initial traffic, prefetch_limit <= 0.5%.
- Tranche 2 – ramp: 24–48h, 60–100% depending on metrics, reduce prefetch to steady-state config.

Risk matrix and mitigations:
- KV eviction storm: if eviction/sec > 5x baseline -> immediately disable prefetching + increase admission threshold. Rehydrate critical prefixes via sampled prewarm using top-1k prefixes from shadow logs.
- GPU saturation due to batching collapse: if average batch size drops by >30% and GPU util spikes, reduce concurrency_limit per-host and enable request coalescing via prefix grouping.
- Unbounded session fanout (unexpected long sessions): enforce session TTL and aggressive prefix TTL clamp (default 6h -> clamp to 1h for new model).

Retrospective metrics to collect during first 72h:
- Actual warmed prefixes (count + bytes) vs predicted.
- KV hit rate delta pre/post rollout.
- Eviction/sec time-series and per-host hotkeys.
- Percent of requests served from fallback quantized variants.
- Mean and tail GPU queue wait times.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Need a calibrated estimate for effective KV entry size for the new model's tokenization (action: research tokenizer payload, @Alyssa).
- Should we enable cross-region prefetching for low-traffic regions? Pro: faster warmup. Con: cross-region bandwidth + GDPR concerns. (Discuss w/ legal).
- Validate whether session hang_time = 2.5m is reasonable for beta customers; update model.

Notes to self / quick commands:
- To run local shadow warmup: infra/tools/shadow-warmup --model new-model --region eu1 --duration 6h --out ./shadow/eu1-newmodel.json
- Prefetch controller flags in prod: --prefetch_limit --prefetch_concurrency --prefetch_backoff_ms

Appendix: sample conservative parameter set (copy-paste for infra team):
- REGION_CAPACITY_HEADROOM_PERCENT=20
- PREFETCH_LIMIT_FRAC=0.005
- SOFT_QUEUE_LATENCY_PCT=90
- SOFT_QUEUE_WAIT_SECONDS=10
- FALLBACK_QUANTIZED_MODEL_ID=new-model-q4_0
- HARD_THROTTLE_GPU_UTIL_PCT=92

Last-minute reminders:
- Coordinate on-call windows with SRE and product eng for tranche 1.
- Add an incident playbook stub on Confluence linking to this file.

References and links:

- Confluence: infra/model-rollout-guidelines
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2897 (admission controller changes)
